newsitem.title: USA: Standard Fed sees no immediate staff cuts.
newsitem.headline: Standard Fed sees no immediate staff cuts.

text.p: Standard Federal Bancorp Inc said Friday it expects no staffing changes among its 4,000 Michigan employees in 1997 following the bank's purchase by ABN AMRO Holding NV.
However, there will be studies to determine where efficiencies can be gained, and some consolidation of back office functions and staff is expected over time, the company said.
"In conducting due dihere will be studies done," said Mike Maher, senior vice president and controller of Standard Federal.
"I don't think you'll notice anything in 1997 as far as any changes in the employee situation," said Maher, who stressed no decisions had been made.

ABN AMRO, an Amerstam-based banking firm with several operations in Chicago, announced Friday it plans to buy all of outstanding Standard Federal's common stock for $59 a share in cash. Total value of the deal is about $1.9 billion.

After the deal closed, Scott Heitman, president and chief executive officer of ABN AMRO's LaSalle Community Bank Group in Chicago, would assume those roles for Standard Federal Bank, the main operating unit of the parent company.
Current Standard Federal Chairman, President and CEO Thomas Ricketts will remain chairman of Standard Federal Bank and become a member of Lasalle Bank FSB's board of directors.

The deal is expected to close by the middle of 1997, pending regulatory and shareholder approvals. Once that happenned, current Standard Federal Bank branches would continue to operate under the Standard Federal name. Standard Federal would remain a stand-alone federal savings bank based in Troy. The company, which was founded in 1893, had assets of $15.5 billion, deposits of $10.8 billion and $10.1 billion of loans serviced for others as of October 31.

Standard Federal's 4,000 employees work at 182 banking centers and 11 home lending centers in Michigan, Indiana, Northwest Ohio and Illinois. The firm's mortgage operation, including InterFirst, a wholesale mortgage banking unit, is the largest thrift lender in the country.
Once combined with ABN AMRO's LaSalle Home Mortgage Corp, joint operations will comprise the country's eighth largest mortgage originator, the firms said.
"With this sale, we'll have immediate acces to a full range of commercial products and services that would otherwise take us years to build," Ricketts said in a statement.
Given the consolidation occurring in the banking industry, Maher said Standard Federal's board had a fiduciary duty to respond to serious offers for the company.
"If you look at the pricing of the deal, it is very fully and fairly priced," he said.
The stock price hit an all-time high of 58 on Thursday. The stock, which fell 1-1/2 to 56-1/2 Friday, has a 52-week low of 36-1/2.
